messages:
kayla: FYI customer-rep reported 504s around 11:45 PST during a tenant burst. Looks like requests queued then timed out while pods were starting. escalation from CS.
mike: any obvious errors in gateway logs?
kayla: gateway shows a bunch of 502/504 with upstream connect timeout. snippets: 
```
ERROR upstream connect timeout service=tenant-gateway path=/v1/generate status=504
```

Also saw repeated 429s from the quota proxy right before.
juan: pulled autoscaler events: KEDA scaled object showed rapid scale-down earlier, then scale-up stalled. Events: `Scaled to 0 -> 1` then `Failed to get trigger auth` several times.
mike: can you paste KEDA controller logs around that window?
juan: pasted minimal excerpt: 
```
E0309 11:44:02 scaler.go:145] failed to get trigger auth for scaledobject tenant-abc: 401 token expired
I0309 11:44:05 scaler.go:210] initiating scale up to 4
I0309 11:44:07 k8s: creating pod tenant-abc-7fd
W0309 11:44:15 podwatcher.go:98] pod pending: ImagePullBackOff (cache-prewarm disabled)
```

juan: TL;DR: token fetch to billing/auth service returned 401 (auth rotation), KEDA couldn't read metric, defaulted to no scaling for ~20s, then pods created but image pull/cache miss added ~40s extra.
nathan: customer impacted: high-latency interactive customers complaining, one support ticket escalated. They saw 30s -> 120s latencies then timeouts.
mike: reproducer we used: `wrk -t4 -c50 -d30s http://gateway/tenant/abc/v1` with a cold cluster and a scaledown to 0. Behavior: queue growth, then 504 once queue hits proxy timeout.
juan: immediate mitigations: 1) bump KEDA controller retry/backoff to avoid auth transient failures causing no-scale; 2) add a short-lived emergency autoscale override for tenant-abc `kubectl scale deployment tenant-abc --replicas=3` to drain queue; 3) re-enable image cache-prewarm for on-demand nodes.
kayla: also opened a support playbook run: created incident INC-2026-3842 and added customer notes. Notifying billing/auth team about token rotation.
mike: patch suggestion: if KEDA auth fails, fallback to HPA based on queue-length metric instead of no-op. This would prevent complete failure when one trigger auth is flaky.
juan: agree. We can also reduce gateway upstream connect timeout from 60s -> 90s as temporary to buy more time during scale.
nathan: told customer we have a mitigation in flight and ETA ~15-30m. They asked for root cause updates.
kayla: Action list: 
- juan: add fallback to HPA on trigger auth failure (PR + test)
- mike: change gateway upstream timeout and deploy canary
- infra-bot: run emergency scale command for tenant-abc now (already executed)
- nathan: update CS ticket with repro steps and ETA

infra-bot: executed: `kubectl scale deployment tenant-abc --replicas=3 --record` at 2026-03-09T11:49:10Z :white_check_mark:
mike: after emergency scale we saw queue drain and 200s resume. Still want follow-up to prevent recurrence.
juan: next steps: audit recent templating change that disabled prewarm cache; rotate KEDA auth integration to avoid 401s during rotation window; add playbook snippet for quick scale override.
kayla: assigning owners on the incident doc. Will schedule postmortem once stabilized. :mag:
